The Luhn rule: starting from the rightmost digit, double every second digit (the second from the right, the fourth, and so on), subtracting 9 from any doubled value above 9; the number is valid when the sum of all the digits so treated is a multiple of 10. def luhn_valid(s):
    # Remove spaces
    s_clean = s.replace(' ', '')
    # Check that all characters are digits
    if not s_clean.isdigit():
        return False
    # Check at least two digits
    if len(s_clean) < 2:
        return False
    # Convert to list of digits
    digits = [int(c) for c in s_clean]
    # Luhn algorithm: starting from rightmost, double every second digit
    # We'll process from right to left, doubling digits at odd indices (0-indexed from right)
    total = 0
    for i, d in enumerate(reversed(digits)):
        if i % 2 == 1:  # every second digit from right (0-indexed: positions 1, 3, 5, ...)
            doubled = d * 2
            if doubled > 9:
                doubled -= 9
            total += doubled
        else:
            total += d
    return total % 10 == 0
